topic_definitions.title: Random matchings
topic_definitions.description: Matchings of random point samples, transportation costs and the discrepancy bounds behind them.

claims.summary: Talagrand's ultimate matching conjecture (Conjecture 5.8 of The Status of my favorite problems): for alpha_1, alpha_2 in (0,infinity] with 1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2=1/2 and a universal L, with probability tending to one as N grows, two independent samples X, Y of N i.i.d. uniform points of [0,1]^2 admit a matching pi with sum_i exp[(sqrt(N/log N)|X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)|/L)^alpha_j] <= 2N for j=1,2; alpha=infinity means max_i |X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)| <= L sqrt(log N/N). Research Problem 17.1.2 of Upper and Lower Bounds for Stochastic Processes (2nd ed., 2021) states it with Y evenly spread, a sufficient form by lem:two-sample-matching-transfer.
claims.assessment: Open conjecture, imported from its two sources with their read statements. Known in the monograph's setting: the pair (alpha,infinity) for alpha<1/2 with constant K(alpha) (Theorem 17.1.3), and the pair (2,2) with constant sqrt(L) but only with probability 9/10 (Talagrand-Yukich), not with probability tending to one; the three-dimensional analogue with exponent sum 1 is Theorem 18.1.1.
claims.rationale: The goal of the ultimate-matching notebook.
claims.next_action: Derive the matching-from-discrepancy reduction for a general exponent pair and identify the class whose discrepancy bound would give it.

claims.summary: For N>=2, alpha in (0,infinity] and point sequences X,Y,Z of length N: if sigma_1 matches X to Z and sigma_2 matches Y to Z with sum_i exp[(sqrt N|P_i^j-Z^j|/(L sqrt(log N)))^alpha] <= 2N (or the maximum bound L sqrt(log N/N) at alpha=infinity), then sigma_2^-1 sigma_1 matches X to Y with the same bound at constant max(2,2^(1/alpha))L. Hence an evenly-spread matching theorem holding with probability 1-eps_N gives the two-sample one with probability 1-2eps_N, no independence of the samples assumed.
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof: triangle inequality, convexity of t^alpha (alpha>=1) or its subadditivity (alpha<1), arithmetic-geometric mean, union bound. Only this direction; the converse is not addressed.
claims.rationale: Shows the monograph's form of the ultimate matching conjecture implies the survey's two-sample form with constant 2L, and transfers Theorem 17.1.3 to two samples.
claims.next_action: Decide whether the two-sample form implies the evenly-spread form, if a later step needs it.

claims.summary: If a matching pi of point sequences satisfies sum_i exp[(sqrt N|X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)|/(L sqrt(log N)))^alpha_j] <= 2N, N>=2, then max_i |X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)| <= L sqrt(log N)(log 2N)^(1/alpha_j)/sqrt N, and for alpha_j>=1 the coordinate distances sum to at most 2L sqrt(N log N). At alpha_1=alpha_2=4 the Euclidean distances have sum <= 4L sqrt(N log N) and maximum <= 4L(log N)^(3/4)/sqrt N; at (2,infinity) Shor's two bounds hold with 2L.
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof (each summand at least 1; t <= exp(t^alpha) for alpha>=1); records with constants the deductions both sources sketch.
claims.rationale: Shows the conjecture contains the Ajtai-Komlos-Tusnady, Leighton-Shor and Shor bounds and the simultaneous sum-and-maximum question.
claims.next_action: None beyond use in later entries.

claims.summary: For X i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2 and Y evenly spread, and any alpha_1, alpha_2 in (4,infinity] and L'>0, it is false that with probability tending to one some matching satisfies sum_i exp[(sqrt N|X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)|/(L' sqrt(log N)))^alpha_j] <= 2N (maximum bound at infinity) for j=1,2. So the diagonal exponent 4 of the ultimate matching conjecture cannot be raised in the evenly-spread setting.
claims.assessment: Working proof from the stated Leighton-Shor upper bound in probability (Theorem 4.7.1) and lower bound in expectation (Theorem 4.8.1) of the monograph: a reverse-Markov step gives the lower bound with probability bounded below; argument proposed by the reviewer and checked. Evenly-spread setting only; off-diagonal pairs with one exponent at most 4 are not addressed.
claims.rationale: Shows the conjecture cannot be strengthened on its diagonal in the monograph's evenly-spread setting.
claims.next_action: Seek an anisotropic Leighton-Shor lower bound to test pairs with exponent sum below 1/2 and one exponent at most 4.

relationships: Carries the monograph's evenly-spread form to the survey's two-sample form with constant 2L at every admissible pair.
Derives the maximum and sum bounds, and the special cases (4,4) and (2,infinity), from the conjecture's conclusion.
Uses part (a), the maximum bound, for exponents at least 1.
Shows no pair with both exponents above 4 holds in the evenly-spread form, so the conjecture is sharp on its diagonal there.
